source_title: India Uttarakhand Helicopter Crash: All 6 On Board Killed, Bodies Recovered
source_excerpt:
A helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt. Ltd. and flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara in Dehradun crashed after losing contact over the Joshimath valley on Friday, killing all six people on board, including the pilot.
The helicopter, bearing call sign VT-HCX, took off at approximately 1:14 pm. Communication with the aircraft was lost while it was flying over the Joshimath valley. Its tracking signal also disappeared, and its location could not be ascertained.
The bodies of all six people, including the pilot, have since been recovered from the crash site, according to an update. Joint teams of the Indian Army, Chamoli district administration, police and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) are carrying out rescue operations. Efforts are underway to transport the bodies from the remote crash site to the nearest road.
As a precautionary measure, the entire fleet of Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt. Ltd. has been grounded, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) said.
According to UCADA, six people, including the pilot, were on board the helicopter.
The pilot has been identified as Captain Himanshu. The five passengers were Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K and HS Natraja.
An investigation has been launched to establish the cause of the crash. Speaking to ABP Ganga at the Sahastradhara helipad, an aviation official said the exact reason would be known only after a detailed probe.
Prateek Jain, CEO of the aviation company, said weather conditions are checked before flights take off. However, investigators will examine whether adverse weather, a technical fault in the helicopter or pilot error contributed to the crash.
He said the findings would be shared after the investigation is completed.
The incident has once again brought helicopter operations during the Char Dham Yatra under scrutiny. The Uttarakhand government has maintained that flights will not be permitted unless weather conditions are clear and that operators are being closely monitored.
A joint team of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and the aviation department is examining the incident from all angles.

hi_body:
ट्रांस भारत एविएशन प्राइवेट लिमिटेड का एक हेलीकॉप्टर शुक्रवार को जोशीमठ घाटी के ऊपर दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हो गया, जिसमें सवार सभी छह लोगों की मौत हो गई। कॉल साइन VT-HCX वाला यह हेलीकॉप्टर बद्रीनाथ से देहरादून के सहस्त्रधारा के लिए दोपहर लगभग 1:14 बजे रवाना हुआ था। उड़ान के दौरान जोशीमठ घाटी के ऊपर संपर्क टूट गया और ट्रैकिंग सिग्नल भी गायब हो गया।

## दुर्घटना और बचाव कार्य
* भारतीय सेना, राज्य आपदा प्रतिक्रिया बल (SDRF), स्थानीय पुलिस और चमोली जिला प्रशासन की संयुक्त टीम ने सभी छह शवों को बरामद कर लिया है।
* शवों को दुर्घटनास्थल से निकटतम सड़क मार्ग तक पहुंचाने के लिए बचाव अभियान जारी है।
* मृतकों में पायलट कैप्टन हिमांशु और पांच यात्री - प्रतापा, अरुण, शंकर गौड़ा, सुधीर के और एचएस नटराज शामिल हैं।

## जांच और आधिकारिक कार्रवाई
उत्तराखंड नागरिक उड्डयन विकास प्राधिकरण (UCADA) ने एहतियाती कदम उठाते हुए ट्रांस भारत एविएशन की पूरी फ्लीट को ग्राउंड कर दिया है। नागर विमानन महानिदेशालय (DGCA) और राज्य विमानन विभाग की एक संयुक्त टीम घटना की जांच कर रही है।

कंपनी के सीईओ प्रतीक जैन ने कहा कि उड़ान भरने से पहले मौसम की जांच की जाती है। हालांकि, जांच में तकनीकी खराबी, खराब मौसम या पायलट की गलती जैसे संभावित कारणों पर गौर किया जाएगा। जांच पूरी होने के बाद ही आधिकारिक निष्कर्ष साझा किए जाएंगे।

en_body:
A helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt. Ltd. crashed in the Joshimath valley on Friday, resulting in the deaths of all six individuals on board. The aircraft, with call sign VT-HCX, lost communication and disappeared from tracking shortly after departing from Badrinath at 1:14 pm, heading toward Sahastradhara in Dehradun.

## Incident Details and Rescue
* The bodies of the six victims have been recovered by joint teams comprising the Indian Army, SDRF, local police, and the Chamoli district administration.
* Recovery operations are ongoing to transport the bodies from the remote crash site to the nearest accessible road.
* The victims include the pilot, Captain Himanshu, and five passengers identified as Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K, and HS Natraja.

## Investigation and Official Response
Following the incident, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) has grounded the entire fleet of Trans Bharat Aviation Pvt. Ltd. A formal investigation is being conducted by a joint team from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and the state aviation department.

Company CEO Prateek Jain stated that while weather conditions are routinely assessed prior to departure, the investigation will now examine potential factors including technical malfunctions, adverse weather, or pilot error. Official findings are expected to be released following the completion of the probe.
